children: Sen.
Elizabeth Warren
(D-Mass.) expressed optimism on Sunday that Democrats would win the November midterms despite the growing influence of “dark money.”
Anonymous Money Entering Elections?
Warren said in an X post that dark money groups have spent “record sums” in this year’s elections.

Roughly $1 billion in anonymous funds has shaped 2026 races, according to a New York Times analysis of ad data, filings and tax records. The report found that secret funding has influenced or is expected to influence “every major primary and battleground race.”
Dark money groups are pouring record sums into our elections.
But the 2026 primaries have shown that when people organize and show up, billionaires don’t get to decide who wins. Grassroots power still matters. And we will in November.
‘We Will Win in November’
Warren said that “grassroots” progressive candidates have succeeded despite the powerful influence of wealthy donors.
Notably,
Abdul El-Sayed
won Michigan’s Senate primary by narrowly defeating Rep.
Haley Stevens
(D-MI) by less than one percentage point.
El-Sayed’s “grassroots” campaign

Democrats were the frontrunners to take control of the House, with 91% odds. The Senate race was closer, with the blue party holding a 61% chance of reclaiming control.
The Republicans currently controls both the House and the Senate. The midterm elections are scheduled for Nov. 3.
